stubs.service: Rath demo datasets on Aliyun OSS (https://chspace.oss-cn-hongkong.aliyuncs.com/api/*.json), which the production build fetches from the 'Demo' data-source tab
stubs.how: The boot loader (out/__seed/boot.js, outside the app source) wraps window.fetch and redirects those URLs to the same files bundled in the build under /datasets/ (bike_dc-dataset-service.json, which isn't bundled, maps to the bundled Washington D.C. bike-sharing dataset ds-bikesharing-service.json)

stubs.service: vega-lite world-110m topojson (https://vega.github.io/vega-lite/data/world-110m.json) used by geo charts
stubs.how: The same fetch wrapper serves a local copy from /__seed/geo/world-110m.json

stubs.service: Persisted user data (Rath keeps the dataset history in the browser's IndexedDB via localforage)
stubs.how: On first load, out/__seed/boot.js writes the datasets from /__seed/rath-seed.json into IndexedDB 'rath_storage_instance' (stores 'meta' + 'datasource'), using the same record shape as Rath's setDataStorage(). It sets localStorage 'rath:ui-capture-seed' so this only runs once, then imports the real app entry

inject() in main.tsx loads /_vercel/insights/script.js, which only Vercel's hosting serves. build.sh copies a local no-op stand-in (.ui-capture/stubs/_vercel/insights/script.js) to out/_vercel/insights/script.js. It drains the window.vaq queue and replaces window.va with a no-op, so nothing is sent

stubs.service: Kanaries gateway (database connector, https://gateway.kanaries.net), Airtable API, causal server (causal.gateway.kanaries.net)
stubs.how: Not stubbed. They are only called when the user sets up a new database or Airtable connection, or picks a server-side causal algorithm. The main UI and analysis (AutoPilot, Copilot, Painter, Dashboard, browser-side causal discovery) run in-browser web workers

app.notes: Rath is a client-only React/Vite SPA with no backend for its main features. Tools are pinned in mise.toml (node 24.11.1, yarn 1.22.22). Built with ./.ui-capture/build.sh, which runs the repo's `yarn build` steps (utils tsc -> vega-scenegraph rollup -> vega-renderer rollup -> rath-client vite build), copies packages/rath-client/build to .ui-capture/out, and routes index.html's entry script through /__seed/boot.js (data-app points at the real entry). Install workarounds for the sandbox: yarn runs with HOME=.ui-capture/home through a $TMPDIR symlink because the sandbox denies reading ~/.npmrc; yarn.lock entries that pointed at registry.npmmirror.com were rewritten to registry.npmjs.org; three tarballs (serialize-javascript 4.0.0, concurrently 4.1.2, iconv-lite 0.6.3) were repacked without .vscode/.idea folders, which the sandbox won't let anything write, and their lockfile hashes were updated. All tarballs sit in the yarn offline mirror .ui-capture/vendor (.yarnrc). Seed data (generator: .ui-capture/seed/gen-seed.mjs) is the dataset history of an analyst at a DTC outdoor-gear retailer after about 11 months of use: 17 datasets with edit times spread from today back to about 9 months ago, so the history groups Today / Week / Month / 3 months / 6 months / Year all fill. Three datasets are pinned with colour tags. They include e-commerce orders (2,400 rows), Airtable support tickets (940, mixed Open/Pending/Solved/Closed), web sessions from a REST API (3,000), Trail Club churn (1,250), weekly marketing spend (498), Postgres inventory snapshot, plant sensor readings, checkout A/B test, store traffic with lat/long, an employee pulse survey with short and long free-text comments, HR headcount, a messy PO export (mixed date formats, inconsistent vendor casing, blanks), a 2024 sales archive, and four of Rath's own demo datasets loaded earlier. They carry the tags @file, @air_table, @restful, @database and @demo. The app opens on the Data Connection page, which shows this history. Click any dataset to load it; the Data Source page then shows the table, meta and stats views, and the left nav opens AutoPilot (megaAuto), Copilot (semiAuto), Manual exploration (GraphicWalker), Painter, Dashboard designer, Collection, Dashboard and Causal analysis. Seeding runs once per browser profile; to re-seed, clear site data or remove localStorage 'rath:ui-capture-seed'.

prompt:
This is a checkout of Kanaries/Rath (https://github.com/Kanaries/Rath) at commit dc54fd90fd77. Next generation of automated data exploratory analysis and visualization platform.

I want to see its user interface in a desktop browser, in the state a real, established user would see it. Please get the app running locally with its main interface working and realistic data in it.

# Running it
- Follow the repo's own setup docs and tooling. Take the simplest route that shows the real app: a static production build if the front end works without a backend, otherwise the app's own server (production or dev mode).
- If it needs a database or other services, run them locally with an embedded or file-based option (SQLite, in-memory, JSON files, an embedded Postgres such as PGlite) or the app's demo/mock mode.
- Don't redesign or restyle anything. Change only what's needed to build and run it.

# Tools: use mise
Install every runtime and tool you need (node, the package manager, python, bun, ...) with mise, pinned to exact versions in a mise.toml at the repo root, so the setup can be reproduced. Match what the repo asks for (engines, .nvmrc, .tool-versions, packageManager). mise is already configured for this directory: `mise install` installs into ./.ui-capture/mise, and its shims come first on PATH, so `node`, `pnpm` and the rest resolve to the pinned versions. Don't use other copies of these tools or download runtimes by hand.

# Secrets, API keys and external services: fake them
The app must not depend on anything outside this machine, and when it runs it has no network except localhost. Wherever it expects secrets, environment variables, API keys or third-party services (hosted auth or OAuth, payment providers, email, LLM or other AI APIs, maps, storage buckets, analytics, hosted databases):
- Give the required variables placeholder values so the app starts.
- Where it actually calls the service, make the call succeed locally with realistic responses: use the app's own mock, test or offline mode if it has one; otherwise point the client at a small local stub server that start.sh also starts, or swap in a stub at the integration boundary (the API client or service module). Keep stubs out of UI code. Responses should look like what the real service returns for a real user, e.g. an AI reply that actually answers, a payment history with real-looking amounts.
- Calls the browser makes directly to outside services count too; point them at the local stub.
- For sign-in through an outside provider, create a local account or use the app's dev sign-in so you can get past it.
List every stub in app.json.

# Data: like real use
Seed it the way an established user's data would look after months of actual use: specific, plausible names and content for this kind of app; dates spread over time; a realistic mix of states (done, in progress, overdue, archived, ...); realistic volume (dozens to hundreds of records where the app revolves around records); short and long text; some messiness real data has. Start from the app's own demo or seed data if it has realistic data, and extend it if it's thin. Load data through the app's own paths (its API, import, seed scripts, or its database schema), never by hardcoding it into UI code. If the app needs an account, create one and attach the data to it. No lorem ipsum or "Test 1".

# Environment
This shell is sandboxed: you can write only inside this directory (package-manager caches already point into ./.ui-capture/cache), and the network reaches only package registries, mise's download sources and GitHub (registry.npmjs.org, registry.yarnpkg.com, repo.yarnpkg.com, github.com, codeload.github.com, objects.githubusercontent.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, nodejs.org, mise.jdx.dev, mise-versions.jdx.dev, release-assets.githubusercontent.com, pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org, binaries.prisma.sh, cdn.jsdelivr.net, unpkg.com). Docker isn't available. A process you start in the background can't be seen or stopped from a later command, so test servers on another port than 4460 (e.g. 5460) or in the foreground under `timeout`; anything still listening on 4460 is stopped before I check.

# When you're done, leave this in ./.ui-capture/
- app.json: {"mode": "static" or "server", "entry": "/path where the main UI opens", "login": null or {"username": "...", "email": "...", "password": "..."}, "stubs": [{"service": "what was faked", "how": "how"}], "notes": "how you set it up, what data is loaded, and the main areas of the app"}
- static mode: the production build in ./.ui-capture/out, with index.html as its entry. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server; unknown paths fall back to index.html.
- server mode: ./.ui-capture/start.sh, which starts everything the app needs (stubs included) in the foreground and serves the UI at http://localhost:4460/ (it gets PORT=4460). It runs with the same PATH and restrictions as your shell, plus no network at all except localhost, so everything must already be installed, built and seeded (or seeded by start.sh itself).
- Put any scripts you write for seeding or stubbing in ./.ui-capture/ too; they're kept with the setup record.

# Order of work
You have 90 minutes in total, and anything unfinished when time runs out is lost. So work in this order:
1. Get the app building and running with its stubs, and write the contract above (app.json plus out/ or start.sh), even if it has only a little data so far.
2. Then build out the data, re-running your seed and checking the app still loads after each substantial step, so that a working state with the data loaded so far is always in place.
Write large data sets with a short generator script rather than as one long literal file.

I'll open it at 1440×900.
